phase: ## Phase S5: Page proofs for Daniel
summary: FAIL: 1 Blocker and 8 nonblocking findings (2 Major, 6 Nit) at head 8ae1bb25. I viewed all 32 page tiles of proof round 8 (Quest 5: 15 pages; Adventure 9.2: 17 pages). PM decisions 2 and 3 hold; decision 1 holds in Quest 5 and holds in part in Adventure 9.2. The Blocker: step 11 (Guided Writing) prints its header alone on a near-empty page in both lessons. The shell refused one command, so I ran no more shell work (PM rule). The verdict does not depend on the measures that I did not run.
blocking_findings: UX2-1 [Blocker] ux-browser-review: The step 11 header (Guided Writing) prints alone on Quest 5 page 11 and Adventure 9.2 page 13. Each of the two pages holds 7 words (the medal, the title, the time chip, and the page number), and the rest of the page is blank. The box starts on the next page (Quest 5 page 12, Adventure page 14). This breaks spec S3 (spec.md line 72): the title and the box must stay on one page. Round 5 kept both on one page, and rounds 6, 7, and 8 show the defect. Daniel needs no question, because this is a defect and not a taste choice.
nonblocking_findings: UX2-2 [Major] ux-browser-review: The self-assessment strip (Excellent 5/5, Good 4/5, Review needed 3 or less) prints at the top of Quest 5 page 8 and Adventure 9.2 page 10. It sits above the step 8 header and away from the MY SCORE box, which stays on the page before (Quest 5 page 7, Adventure page 9). Round 5 kept the strip and the score box on one page, and rounds 6, 7, and 8 split them. A child sees three tick boxes with no score box beside them. Fix: keep the strip with the score box, for example with a keep rule on both. Route: Green, in the same round as UX2-1.

UX2-3 [Major] ux-browser-review: PM decision 1 holds for Quest 5 and holds in part for Adventure 9.2. On Adventure 9.2 page 3 the hero prints at 84.7 mm, but a block of 84.2 x 72.2 mm right of the hero holds no ink. Paragraph 1 starts on page 4, so only the reading key sits beside the hero. On Quest 5 page 3 the text starts 14.1 mm right of the hero, and the old 35.3 mm strip is closed. Fix: let paragraph 1 start beside the hero and continue on page 4, or ask Daniel to accept the white space (question 1). Route: Green if the PM wants decision 1 met in the long lesson.

UX2-4 [Nit] ux-browser-review: The page number of page 1 prints 5.3 mm lower than on the other pages, in both lessons. The lowest word on page 1 ends at 276.1 mm, and on the other pages it ends at 270.8 mm. The page 1 content also starts about 5 mm lower (25.4 mm against 20.3 mm). The number stays 9 mm from the trim edge, so it is not clipped. Daniel may notice the jump when he turns from page 1 to page 2.

UX2-5 [Nit] ux-browser-review: In the Guided Writing frame, the Sentence Starters box and the QR panel touch the frame sides. The frame edge looks thicker there, and the bottom shows two borders about 4 mm apart. This reads as a double border. The markup comes from the shared template, and the earlier rounds did not flag it. I saw it on the 178 dpi render of Quest 5 page 12, and Adventure page 14 uses the same markup.

UX2-6 [Nit] ux-browser-review: The pages still leave large blank areas and widow cards (earlier finding UX-5, unchanged). One vocabulary card stands alone at the top of Quest 5 page 3, and two cards stand alone at the top of Adventure 9.2 page 3. The blank area at the page foot is about 65 to 115 mm on Quest 5 pages 6, 8, 9, and 13, and on Adventure pages 4, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11, and 15 (tile estimates, error about 2 mm). The page rules of primary_template.html cause this, and this phase did not change them. Daniel decides whether he wants fuller pages (question 4).

UX2-7 [Nit] ux-browser-review: The card edges still print in the pale parchment-2 tone (earlier finding UX-6, unchanged). The vocabulary cards, the write-in wells, and the planner boxes use a 2 px edge in #e9d4a8. The contrast of this edge on white is about 1.5 to 1, so it looks faint on the tiles. The earlier review found a darker edge on the app cards. Daniel decides whether he wants a darker edge (question 2).

UX2-8 [Nit] ux-browser-review: Two Thai details remain for Daniel's Thai check (earlier finding UX-7). In the Adventure 9.2 translation (page 17), the polite closing word of paragraph 2 wraps alone onto its own line. The Latin words 'STAFF ONLY' in paragraph 3 print in a light weight, and they look thinner than the Thai text. The Thai glosses now print upright, so the italic point of UX-7 is closed. I saw no clipped or missing mark in the 178 dpi render of Adventure page 17, and the earlier round checked the marks at 300 dpi.

UX2-9 [Nit] ux-browser-review: The contact sheets still pair no app capture with printed steps 9, 10, and 11 (earlier finding UX-8). The pages tsv files show no capture for Quest 5 pages 9 to 12 and Adventure pages 11 to 14, and Quest 5 page 5 pairs step 4 only. Step-map.ts maps printed steps 9 and 10 to app steps 9 to 12, and those captures exist. I read the tsv files in this round, and I did not open the contact sheets. Route: the proof driver author.

UX2-1 fix guidance (for Green; this role edits no product file): the rule .guided-writing-step has break-before: page (primary_template.html line 580), so the header always starts a page. Shrink the pair by at least 5 mm. Keep the 8 mm line pitch. Options: remove the 4 mm top margin on that header (a page break already precedes it), trim the planner spacing, or let the box split after its header. Cutting the draft lines from 6 to 5 saves 8 mm but touches decision 2, so the PM must choose. Add check P18: the step 11 header and its box start on the same page in both lessons.
